content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Cemiplimab dose inconsistency between synopsis and body",
      "quote": "cemiplimab will be administered intravenously (IV) as a flat dose of 437 mg every 3 weeks (Q3W)",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "Synopsis Study Design",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The synopsis Study Design states a flat dose of 437 mg Q3W, but the Treatments section of the same synopsis states 350 mg Q3W. This is a critical dosing discrepancy that must be resolved.",
      "fix": "Reconcile the cemiplimab dose to a single value (e.g., 350 mg Q3W) and ensure consistency throughout the protocol."
    },
  {
      "title": "Sample size inconsistency between synopsis sections",
      "quote": "Approximately 708 patients will be randomized",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "Synopsis Study Design",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The Study Design states approximately 708 patients will be randomized, but the Population section states approximately 460 SCC patients and approximately 590 overall. These numbers are irreconcilable and need clarification.",
      "fix": "Clarify the total sample size and the relationship between SCC and overall populations."
    },
  {
      "title": "Interim analysis results and amendment not described in body",
      "quote": "The second interim analysis demonstrated survival advantage for patients treated with cemiplimab over IC chemotherapy. As such, Amendment 7 will allow for an cemiplimab Extension Phase.",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "Synopsis Study Design",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The synopsis mentions a second interim analysis and Amendment 7, but the body text provided does not include details of the interim results, the amendment, or the extension phase design. This is a significant gap.",
      "fix": "Add a section describing the interim analysis results, Amendment 7 changes, and the cemiplimab Extension Phase design."
    },
  {
      "title": "Contraception requirements missing",
      "quote": "pregnancy test for women of childbearing potential",
      "page": 29,
      "section": "Synopsis Procedures and Assessments",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol mentions pregnancy testing but lacks any contraception requirements for patients or partners, which is essential for a study of a potentially teratogenic chemotherapy and an investigational immunotherapy.",
      "fix": "Add a contraception section specifying requirements for women of childbearing potential and male patients with partners of childbearing potential."
    },
  {
      "title": "Trial stopping rules not described",
      "quote": "Two interim efficacy analyses are planned using Lan-DeMets (O’Brien-Fleming) spending function at 70% and 85% of the total OS events",
      "page": 30,
      "section": "Synopsis Statistical Plan",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The statistical plan describes interim analyses for efficacy but does not mention any stopping rules for futility, safety, or other reasons. The M11 template requires a dedicated section on trial stopping rules.",
      "fix": "Add a section on trial stopping rules, including criteria for early stopping for efficacy, futility, or safety."
    },
  {
      "title": "Access to trial intervention after end of trial not described",
      "quote": "Patients randomized to IC chemotherapy will have the option to receive monotherapy with cemiplimab.",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "Synopsis Study Design",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The synopsis mentions an extension phase during the trial, but there is no description of post-trial access to cemiplimab after the study ends. This is required by M11 section 4.5.",
      "fix": "Add a section describing post-trial access to cemiplimab or state that none is planned."
    },
  {
      "title": "Primary objective wording is ambiguous",
      "quote": "The primary objective is to compare overall survival (OS) for patients with recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer who have histology of squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) and who have any eligible histology",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "Synopsis Objectives",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary objective is poorly worded, making it unclear whether the primary analysis is in SCC patients only or in all eligible histologies. The statistical plan clarifies that OS is tested in SCC first, but the objective should be rewritten for clarity.",
      "fix": "Rewrite the primary objective to clearly state that OS is compared in SCC patients first, and then in the overall population if the SCC test is significant."
    },
  {
      "title": "End of trial definition missing",
      "quote": "Study closeout procedures will be implemented following the last patient last visit of the cemiplimab Extension Phase",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "Synopsis Study Design",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The synopsis mentions study closeout but does not define the end of trial (e.g., last patient last visit, database lock, or a specific date). M11 requires a clear definition of end of trial.",
      "fix": "Add a definition of end of trial, such as the date of the last visit of the last patient or another specified event."
    }
  ]
}
